prompt: Thread A locks X then Y. Thread B locks Y then X. Follow one unlucky schedule.

trace.label: A locks X and B locks Y. Now A calls lock(Y). A
B then calls lock(X). B
choices: takes X because it ran earlier
takes X after A is preempted

trace.label: So the program
choices: finishes A first and then B
lets the OS cancel one lock

trace.label: Which rule makes this schedule impossible?
choices: every thread locks X before Y
every thread unlocks before it locks

explain: Each thread holds what the other needs, and neither will release until it gets the second lock. A global lock order breaks the cycle: whoever gets X first also gets Y.
